origin.note: A chronological record of transactions using equal debit and credit entries.

theory.definition: A journal records transactions in date order, identifying accounts debited and credited.
theory.purpose: It provides the initial accounting record and an audit trail before ledger posting.
principles: Each transaction has equal debit and credit amounts.
rules: Identify at least two affected accounts.
Record equal total debits and credits.
Post journal lines to the relevant ledger accounts.

posting_steps: Enter equal debit and credit amounts.
Post each line to the ledger.
common_errors: Using the wrong account or date.

exercise.prompt: Record an owner cash contribution and a cash expense.
exercise.answer_rule: Each transaction must have equal debit and credit amounts and preserve the accounting equation.

on_statements: Supplies ledger balances used in later statements.
on_decisions: Review transaction history and trace unusual entries.
risk_if_wrong: Misclassification or omission can flow into later reports.

depth.level_1: A dated record of transactions showing equal debits and credits.
depth.level_2: Analyze each event, select accounts, enter both sides, then post to ledger accounts.
depth.level_3: Adjusting, compound, and correcting entries require additional analysis; compare journal entry capture with cash-book and voucher procedures.
